reasoning: The analysis identifies two primary risk indicators. First, the eligibility criteria (Class-A registration, turnover ≥ ₹100 crore, experience ≥ 15 years) are satisfied by only one of 200 vendors (V-047), indicating tailored eligibility criteria [F-1]. This raises concerns about proportionality: Directive 2014/24/EU requires that selection criteria be appropriate, related and proportionate to the contract subject-matter [KB-002]. The General Financial Rules further state that bidding documents should be self-contained and comprehensive, with eligibility criteria covering experience, turnover and technical capability [KB-012]. The Manual for Procurement of Works recommends turnover thresholds based on a multiplier (2×, not less than 1.5× for large contracts) of projected annual expenditure [KB-015] and experience criteria based on similar works completed in the last seven years [KB-016]; the current 15-year experience and ₹100 crore turnover requirements may not align with these benchmarks. Second, a vendor ring links V-045, V-046 and V-047 through shared address and shared director (score 0.7) [R-1], suggesting possible connections between the sole qualifying vendor and other market participants. No guideline passage in the knowledge base was retrieved in support of ring R-1.
recommended_actions: Escalate this tender to the competent vigilance authority for human examination before any award.
Review the relationships between the linked vendors (V-047) and the other members of their flagged rings.
Hold the tender evaluation until the human reviewer has recorded a conclusion.
Review eligibility criteria for proportionality and alignment with procurement guidelines
Investigate vendor relationships in ring R-1 for potential collusion
Consider revising criteria to ensure broader competition
Assess whether the turnover and experience thresholds are justified by the contract's scale and complexity
